title: GSOFT logical experts from one shared FFN
hypothesis: Sixteen routed GSOFT output Views over one shared FFN can match independent expert functions with lower serialized bytes and modest active compute; same-budget IA3 and rank-one residual controls test whether simpler expert views suffice.
physical_object: one shared FP32 two-layer FFN expert
logical_multiplicity: 16 routed logical experts over one physical FFN
controls: native GSOFT group-shuffle parameterization with identical function

development.selection_metric: per-expert output NRMSE, pairwise diversity, actual bytes, active expert MAC proxy

success_gate: Across all audit seeds, GSOFT expert output NRMSE <=1e-5 and complete payload <=25% independent with active compute <=1.2x at <=2 stages. Compare IA3/rank-one at actual bytes. Native exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: Any audit seed misses quality/bytes/compute gate or IA3/rank-one matches quality at lower bytes/compute. Exact native GSOFT alias rejects Mirror-specific value regardless of generic expert-sharing feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic routed FFN functions only; no expert training, language utility, GPU or serving claim.
Target experts are generated from GSOFT Views by construction; this is not learned capacity evidence.
One routed expert is active per sample and router IDs are serialized and charged.
